chunks: Ahmad narrated from a number of our companions, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Zurara, from one of the progeny of A'ayn, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever was a Believer, he is emancipated after seven years, whether his master emancipates him or does not emancipate him, and it is not permissible to have the services of the one who was a Believer after seven years.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a believing slave after seven years of servitude?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi articulates the principle of 'automatic emancipation' (itq) for believing slaves, emphasizing that faith itself acts as a catalyst for freedom after a seven-year period, regardless of the master's formal declaration. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the intrinsic dignity of the believer and serves as a practical mechanism for gradual manumission, ensuring that a slave's status is not perpetually bound by servitude but is elevated by their spiritual standing.
